item.title: Sparta UFC vet Jim Miller blends family, farming, fighting | Exclusive
item.description: Jim Miller hasn't changed much during his long mixed martial arts career. There might not be butterflies as Miller takes his 48th walk to face Terrance McKinney in UFC's Octagon on Nov. 14 in New York City. But the 43-year-old from Sparta remains just as steady and hardworking as in his pro debut almost exactly 21 years ago. The only one to fight at UFC 100, 200 and 300 , Miller (39-19, 1 NC) holds UFC records for most bouts, wins and submission attempts. He earned his first UFC submission in the third round of his first fight with the organization back in October 2008. "To think back to those beginning days, it's a lifetime ago," Miller said in an exclusive interview on Tuesday, shortly after arriving at a midtown Manhattan hotel for UFC 334 Fight Week. "I'm a competitor. I've been an athlete my whole life. I somehow found a way to continue on into my 40s. Very few people have that opportunity. I've been trying to make the most of it." Quick ending ahead? Miller is 11 years older, two inches shorter, and has a two-inch reach disadvantage against McKinney. But he's not worried about those numbers. His challenge on Saturday at Madison Square Garden is to match McKinney's aggressiveness and power right from the start. McKinney (18-9) has a first-round finish in all but one of his wins. But Miller has 17 first-round finishes of his own. Longtime trainer Brian McLaughlin said Miller's power has increased as he's aged. He believes Miller has the ability to knock McKinney out – quickly – with a hard shot. "Keep your eyes open. They're here for a good time, not a long time," McLaughlin said. "It's different with your pacing. You don't save your energy, because you're saving yourself for a round you're unlikely to see. ... You meet aggression with aggression, get ready for a sprint, and it becomes more instinctual and less strategic." Fighter and family man A wrestler since age 4, he remembers running on the roads in Lake Mohawk with his older brothers to get into shape. They also worked construction with their father, Mike Miller, who Jim called "a mountain of a man" at 6-foot-4 and 240 pounds who would "do physical, athletic things" on a job site and then come home and cook meals for the family. Jim Miller discovered MMA as an eighth grader after sneaking into a Bloomsburg University wrestling camp with his brothers. A coach played a VHS tape of an early UFC fight, and Jim thought, "Man, that's scary. I kind of want to do it." After wrestling at Sparta for four years, Miller dove into UFC online while at Virginia Tech. He and his brother Dan Miller decided to try it out, and both established careers. They also designed, built and opened their own training facility in Sparta in 2014. Now known as Sussex County MMA, that same space still serves as Jim Miller's year-round base. item.title: Local high school athletes make college plans official on National Signing Day
item.description: The De Pere boys basketball team has won five consecutive Fox River Classic Conference championships, and it will be one of the favorites again this season thanks in part to the return of Will Krueger. The league’s reigning player of the year made his collegiate future official Nov. 11 during National Signing Day. The 6-foot-5 senior shooting guard will play for Michigan Tech, an NCAA Division II school in Houghton. The Huskies went 29-7 last season and advanced to the Elite Eight of the NCAA DII Tournament. The 29 wins tied the program record. Some of the best players in program history have been local players, a list highlighted by former Ashwaubenon stars Kyle Monroe and Marcus Tomashek . Krueger should provide Michigan Tech with another solid scorer when he arrives in 2027-28. He has been a key figure for the Redbirds since his sophomore year and averaged a team-high 17.2 points along with 5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1 steal per game as a junior. Krueger shot 46.8% from 3-point range and has made 106 3-pointers in his career. “Will is a great teammate and his leadership will be extremely important to our success this year,” longtime De Pere basketball coach Brian Winchester said in a statement. “Will has worked hard to develop his talents and is very deserving of the opportunity at Michigan Tech. “Our coaching staff is extremely proud of Will and wish him continued success at MTU after a successful senior year and taking a run at another state title.” Krueger is one of several local athletes who will play at an NCAA Division I or II school and are expected to sign their letters of intent this week or next. Ashwaubenon Emma Kozloski will compete in swimming at DII Quincy University in Illinois. The senior will be busy at the WIAA Division 2 state meet this week. She is set to compete in the 100-yard breaststroke and the 200-yard individual medley and was part of 200 freestyle and 400 freestyle relay teams that won sectional championships. Bay Port Karlie Schock will play tennis at the University of Michigan. She made history as a freshman in 2023 when she became the first local D1 girls player to win a state title since the tournament started in 1971 while becoming the first since Racine Case’s Bojana Pozder in 2018 to not drop a single set at state. Schock returned for her sophomore season with hopes of leading Bay Port to state, but when that goal fell short after the Pirates’ runner-up sectional finish, she opted to not defend her state title at the individual tournament and instead compete in a USTA junior event. She did not play high school tennis her final two seasons but is one of the best players in the state. Her commitment to the Wolverines keeps the family tradition alive. Her father, Dr. Harold Schock III, was a standout defenseman on Michigan’s national title hockey team in 1996 and was considered one of the program’s best players of the decade. item.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
item.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. "Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men's first-team head coach," the club said in a statement. "Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions." Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January. But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, the team have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings. Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago, with United yet to win a Premier League title since the retirement of the outstanding Scottish manager. item.title: Liam Lawson retained by Racing Bulls for 2027 alongside Arvid Lindblad
item.description: Motorsport photo Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second year. Lawson and Lindblad formed a formidable duo this year as they propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the constructors' championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result. But despite accounting for 89 points, twice the number rookie Lindblad managed, Lawson's future had been thrown into doubt as Racing Bulls weighed up its need for short-term performance with its explicit goal of training young drivers for its parent team Red Bull Racing. Red Bull has the exciting young Bulgarian prospect Nikola Tsolov, a frontrunner in F2, waiting in the wings, having handed him private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico. But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, delivering some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old New Zealander has been too good for the team to ignore. Sources indicated to Motorsport.com over the Brazilian Grand Prix weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header. Lawson has now signed a fresh deal that will keep him at the team for 2027, with Lindblad afforded a second season after a promising rookie campaign. Team boss Alan Permane said he had "no doubt" the team will field the strongest possible line-up next season. item.description: Florida State football snapped its nearly three-year-long road losing streak with a win over Boston College in the first game of the post-Mike Norvell era . Now, the Seminoles under interim head coach Rick Stockstill are tasked with following it up with a consecutive road win for the first time in nearly three seasons, traveling to a wounded but capable Pitt team on Friday, Nov. 13. The Panthers are coming off a bye week, but beat Georgia Tech 34-11 last time out. Tallahassee Democrat FSU Athletics beat reporter Liam Rooney breaks down the matchup. The Packers are 6-3 this season and the Vikings 6-2 in the NFC North, where every team has at least six wins. item.description: Junior Caminero - Tampa Bay Rays | © X/@RaysBaseball Rays star third baseman Junior Caminero reportedly earned more from his Adidas endorsement deal in 2026 than his pre-arbitration annual salary with Tampa Bay, according to his agent at Republik Sports, Rafael Nieves. According to Spotrac , Caminero earned a base salary of $794,800 for the 2026 campaign while still under a rookie contract. He is not eligible for salary arbitration until 2028. The All-Star third baseman is not set for unrestricted free agency until 2031. “I want to let people know, as we prepare for the lockout, that Adidas paid Junior Caminero more money than the Tampa Bay Rays this season,” Nieves wrote on X while making a bold claim about next year’s potential lockout. Watch the post here: Caminero is coming off a phenomenal season with Tampa Bay , batting .276 with 42 home runs, 101 RBIs, 170 hits, and an .885 OPS. It marked the second consecutive year the 23-year-old hit 40 or more home runs and drove in 100 or more runs during the regular season. In 14 postseason games, he went 13-for-52, with one home run, four extra-base hits, five RBIs, a .250 batting average, and a .700 OPS. After his agent revealed that Adidas paid him more for brand endorsements than his club salary in 2026, the news went viral. Reports from The Big Lead and Sports Illustrated noted that Caminero could command a multi-year contract extension worth $150 million to $300 million. However, the Rays and Caminero’s camp have not yet discussed a long-term deal. item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reveals how he’ll handle reports from Dianna Russini
item.description: ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter has explained how he will approach reports from Dianna Russini following her return to sports media. Schefter made it clear that her recent controversy will not change his reporting process. Russini returned to NFL coverage on Nov. 11 after a seven-month absence. She also launched a new weekly program, The Russini Report, through BetUS. Her return followed her resignation from The Athletic in April. The outlet later concluded that her undisclosed personal relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel violated newsroom standards. MORE: Dianna Russini makes first statement on return to NFL media Speaking on WEEI 93.7 FM, Schefter was asked whether he would trust information reported by Russini. He said he would apply the same verification process used with every other reporter. “I would treat her like everybody else,” Schefter said. “I have to verify everybody’s information before I report it. So, I don’t think of it as anything different. I don’t think of circumstances like that. That’s me. I’m thinking the way I have thought about doing my job, the way I need to do my job, whether it’s Diana Russini or anybody else doing it. “I don’t care who’s doing it. Like, I don’t care who it is. I’m not reporting it until I know that it’s true. Period.” Adam Schefter avoids judging Dianna Russini’s return Westlake Village, CA, USA; Reporter Dianna Russini at Oaks Christian High School. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) The host also asked whether journalists who cross professional boundaries with sources should remain NFL insiders. Schefter declined to make Russini’s situation a broader issue for the profession. He instead returned to his own responsibilities. “I mean, I haven’t thought about it like that,” Schefter said, comparing the situation to criticism surrounding other media professionals. “I do my job, and I’ve got enough to worry about with my own problems and issues. Don’t need to worry about somebody else’s,” he added. “I just try to do my job the right way.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter was on with Rich, Ken, and Ted and talks about trusting any news being reported by Dianna Russini now that she is back. @KenLairdWEEI @teddyjradio @heyrichhey pic.twitter.com/c1TyvFYXtc — WEEI (@WEEI) November 11, 2026 MORE: Giants’ J.J. item.title: ‘Sabotage’ – Dejounte Murray shares and deletes cryptic allegations after poor Pelicans’ performances
item.description: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray made some cryptic comments on social media after the team’s 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets before quickly deleting his post. Murray is a former All-Star guard and used to be touted as one of the best defensive guards in the NBA. However, injuries and ill-fitting team situations have caused his stock to go down over recent seasons, with it crashing in the 2026-27 NBA season. Amid a string of poor performances as a starting guard for the 4-8 Pelicans, Murray seemed to post a cryptic comment on social media before quickly deleting it. Dejounte Murray claims he’s being sabotaged on the Pelicans NBA Central shared a post highlighting that the Pelicans are undefeated in games when Murray was not playing (3-0), going 1-8 when Murray is on the court this season. Murray posted a cryptic quoted message about this stat, referencing sabotage against him by the team, before deleting it within minutes of posting. “From what’s going on inside, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! The sabotage is real!” Murray is explicitly implying that something is wrong within the Pelicans team and that NBA Central was asked to post an unflattering stat about the 30-year-old guard, equating the same to being sabotaged. Murray is averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists this season, but the Pelicans have looked clearly out of sync when he is on the court. In addition, the emergence of second-year guard Jeremiah Fears is leading to reduced responsibilities for Murray. This might be a reference to contract extension talks, as Murray is extension-eligible. His current contract can expire in 2027 if he declines the $30.2 million player option on his deal. He signed this four-year, $114.2 million deal with the Atlanta Hawks before being traded to the Pelicans in 2024. If Murray has a low contract offer from the Pelicans at the moment, it could be understandable why he would think a stat like the one NBA Central shared would lower his value and negotiating power. Murray is making $32.7 million this season. With Fears’ emergence, a potential contract stand-off, and this concerning deleted post situation, it would not be surprising to see Murray available on the trade market closer to February. item.description: Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United , with the club inside the relegation zone during the international break and considering a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos, under Sir Jim Ratcliffe, took control of football operations. Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – saw the goodwill this season evaporate after United’s worst start to a season in 40 years , with a disastrous defensive performance seeing them go two goals down against Aston Villa before a miraculous late comeback earned a 4-4 draw. Liverpool away after the international break offers little hope of escaping the drop zone, before a trip to Lisbon in the Champions League. While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – while criticism of Carrick’s tactics came from United captain Bruno Fernandes , who has not been able to inspire the team in the manner that saw him pick up the PFA Player of the Year award and the league’s assist record last term. So who could be in charge at Anfield and beyond in a bid to, firstly, guide the club away from a relegation battle? Mauricio Pochettino The current odds-on favourite after emerging as a key target , yet Man United could face a problem getting the Argentine out of his United States contract, having committed to terms up to the next World Cup in 2030. Compensation in excess of £7m could follow, yet United are in a desperate situation and the experience and presence of Pochettino could spark a reaction from a group desperately short of inspiration. Pochettino’s powers have waned since his famous spell with Spurs, though his exit at Chelsea came at the end of a promising run to conclude the 2023/24 season. There was immense potential and excitement to start the 2026 World Cup, but a combination of the Folarin Balogun scandal and then a thumping at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 took the shine off Pochettino’s performance from the dugout. Now, it remains to be seen if he can deliver once more in club football in what would surely be his most difficult job to date. item.title: Eintracht Frankfurt make Nottingham Forest outcast Arnaud Kalimuendo top January target after Premier League club approve €30m transfer or loan exit
item.description: Nottingham Forest v Leeds United - Carabao Cup Second Round - Getty Images Sport Eintracht Frankfurt have identified Nottingham Forest striker Arnaud Kalimuendo as their priority attacking target for the upcoming January transfer window. The Premier League outfit are ready to sanction a departure after placing a €30 million valuation on the peripheral Frenchman, while also remaining open to a loan deal. Frustrated striker seeks regular minutes According to TEAMtalk , the 24-year-old is eager to leave the City Ground this winter after falling down the pecking order under head coach Oliver Glasner. Since returning to England for the current campaign, Kalimuendo has been restricted to just 110 minutes across five appearances without registering a single goal or assist. Four of those outings have come off the bench, prompting multiple suitors to circle ahead of the New Year. Midlands hierarchy outline departure terms The report states that the Tricky Trees will not stand in the way of the forward pursuing regular first-team football elsewhere when the mid-season market opens. Having signed him from French side Rennes in August 2025 on a long-term contract running until June 2030, the English club ideally prefer a permanent sale to recoup the €30m fee they originally paid. However, insiders indicate that officials in the East Midlands are realistic about market conditions should no suitor match their full valuation outright in the middle of the season. Consequently, decision-makers are prepared to approve an initial temporary switch provided the agreement includes either an option or an obligation to buy next summer. Productive loan spell fuels interest That flexibility has alerted the Bundesliga outfit, who have continued to monitor the attacker closely following his productive stint in Germany during the second half of last season. Across 19 appearances for the Eagles during that spell, the former Ligue 1 regular found the back of the net six times to leave a lasting impression on the club's hierarchy. With his limited game time under Glasner raising serious doubts over his long-term role in the Premier League, the outlet notes that a winter departure now represents a realistic solution for all parties. Moving back to a familiar environment would give the Frenchman an immediate platform to rediscover his scoring touch during the second half of the campaign. Temporary structure offers realistic solution Although Frankfurt have made re-signing Kalimuendo their top winter objective, financing a €30m permanent transfer mid-season would pose a major financial hurdle. As a result, negotiating a loan arrangement with a future purchase clause represents the most probable route for the German club to conclude a deal. Such an agreement would allow Forest to protect their initial investment while keeping their long-term options open.

item.title: Five things to know about Akron men's soccer before Big East Tournament
item.description: The University of Akron will play Creighton in a Big East Conference men's soccer tournament semifinal at 5 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 12, at the Maryland SportsPlex in Boyds, Md. Akron (11-1-4, 4-1-3) is the No. 3 seed and Creighton (12-1-5, 4-1-3) is the No. 2 seed. No. 1 seed Georgetown (14-1-2, 7-0-1) will play No. 4 seed Seton Hall (7-4-6, 4-2-2) in the second semifinal around 7:30 p.m. Both games will stream live on ESPN+, with the championship match set for 2 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, on ESPNU. Here are five things to know about the Akron men's soccer team . Akron men's soccer closing in on another NCAA Tournament appearance In its 72nd year of competition, the Akron men's soccer team is closing in on its 38th NCAA Tournament appearance. Akron has made six College Cup appearances. The Zips won the 2010 national championship under former coach Caleb Porter , and were national runners-up in 1986 with former coach Steve Parker, in 2009 with Porter and in 2018 with current coach Jared Embick. Akron men's soccer history in conference tournaments Akron is seeking its first Big East Tournament title since joining the conference in soccer only in 2023. This will be Akron's fourth trip to the Big East Tournament after winning 15 Mid-American Conference Tournament championships from 1998-2018. Akron defeated host Marquette 2-0 on Nov. 6 in its regular-season finale to clinch a share of the Big East Conference Midwest Division title. The victory in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, gave the Zips their third consecutive shared or outright division crown in the Big East. Akron takes winning streak into Big East Conference Tournament Akron enters Thursday with four consecutive wins and six wins in its past eight matches since losing 3-1 at home to Georgetown on Sept. 25. The Hoyas were ranked No. 5 in the country then and are now No. 2 behind top-ranked Southern Methodist University. Akron's past eight matches include wins over DePaul (2-0) and Syracuse (2-1), draws against Creighton (1-1) and Providence (1-1) and victories over Cleveland State (3-2), Xavier (2-1), Villanova (5-0) and Marquette (2-0). item.title: 'We absolutely support Pat': Cricket Australia backs Cummins amid fresh Sandpapergate row
item.description: Cricket Australia chairman David Boon has thrown his support behind Test captain Pat Cummins following fresh allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Boon has made it clear that Cummins' position as captain is safe and that the board continues to have full faith in him. The controversy has returned to the spotlight after former Australia batter Usman Khawaja made fresh claims in his autobiography, "Sabr". Khawaja alleged that all members of the Australian team on the 2018 South Africa tour knew about the plan to tamper with the ball. His claims have reopened the debate over the scandal and led to demands for another investigation. Cummins, who now leads Australia's Test team, has also come under pressure to explain what he knew. Boon says Cricket Australia has full faith in Cummins Boon said Cummins had led the team with honesty and had the board's complete backing. “We absolutely support Pat,” Boon said in comments published by The Australian on Thursday. “He’s been an exemplary captain, he’s led the team with integrity and, you know, very successfully over the period of time that he’s been captain, so there’s no question of our confidence in him continuing on in that fact.” Cummins has not yet publicly addressed Khawaja's allegations. He, however, posted on X that he would speak to the media on Friday after going through the claims. "I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly," he wrote. Mitchell Marsh, Australia's white-ball captain, is also expected to address the issue. Marsh was part of the Test team during the 2018 tour and will speak at a press conference in Perth later on Thursday, ahead of the ODI against England. Warner and Sayers support Khawaja's version Khawaja's claims have received support from former teammate David Warner. Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were all banned for their roles in the ball-tampering scandal. Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers, who was also part of the 2018 South Africa tour, has also backed Khawaja. Speaking to Australian media last weekend, Sayers said the allegations were "accurate". Despite the fresh claims, Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday that there was no compelling reason to reopen the investigation. Boon repeated the same position, saying the board did not want to get into a dispute over different versions of events. "I respect (Usman’s) point of view and his recollections of what occurred, and they’re his, but we don’t want to get into a he-said-she-said argument," he said. item.title: Michael Carrick sacked by Man United with club stuck in relegation zone after latest crisis
item.description: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United manager with the club sitting in the Premier League relegation places after 10 games. A second Old Trafford comeback of the week, this time battling from two goals down twice to rescue a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday , could not save Carrick’s job and he departs United just three months into the start of the season and with his side 18th during the international break. United ended a nine-game winless run when they came from two goals down to beat Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday but they have not won in eight attempts in the Premier League and have just one top-flight win this campaign. It represents a stark turnaround from Carrick’s positive impact as interim manager last season, when the former midfielder went beyond expectations after replacing Ruben Amorim in January, steadying the ship and guiding them to Champions League qualification. Carrick’s position has been under threat since the damaging defeats against Como and Bournemouth last month, but he survived crisis talks with the United hierarchy and was given time to turn results around , but speculation over a change begun the day after Sunday’s chaotic draw and United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is expected to succeed Carrick having reportedly reached a verbal agreement with the club. United have made contact with US Soccer over compensation for Pochettino with a reported figure of $10m (£7.4m) set to be paid to release him from his contract which was due to run through to the 2030 World Cup. His current staff are set to join him at Old Trafford and would require further compensation payments. The timing of the November international break, with a full two weeks before their next game away to Liverpool in the Premier League, has prompted United to finally act and leave minority owners Ineos searching for a fourth permanent manager in three years. Though Pochettino is the overwhelming favourite to become the next head coach, Eddie Howe is available following his departure from Newcastle in the summer while former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann is also an option. Aston Villa’s Unai Emery and Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler are admired but their clubs would demand significant compensation. Manchester United confirmed the news of Carrick’s exit with a statement which reads: “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach. “Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period. “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions. “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. item.title: Hawkins, Ponga and Waaka win Golden Boot awards
item.description: Rob Hawkins was named Wheels of Steel winner - English rugby league's wheelchair player of the year - in September [SWPix] England's Rob Hawkins has won the International Rugby League's wheelchair Golden Boot award for the third year running. Hawkins, 25, is the first player in any form of rugby league to win three successive Golden Boots - awarded by the IRL to the best player in the world during the calendar year. He is only the second player in rugby league history, after Australia and Queensland great Johnathan Thurston, to win a Golden Boot three times. New Zealand full-back Kalyn Ponga won the men's Golden Boot award and New Zealand's Stacey Waaka the women's. Hawkins is set to be part of the England team who will seek to retain the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup when they face rivals France in Wollongong, Australia, on Friday at 08:45 GMT. He saw off competition from England team-mate Joe Coyd, plus France trio Jeremy Bourson, Nicolas Clausells and Dany Denuwelaere, to win the award. Ireland captain Joe Calcott and Australia's Bayley McKenna and Adam Tannock were also nominated. Hawkins has scored 19 tries at the World Cup for England, including five as they thrashed Australia 86-28 in Tuesday's semi-final. Ponga, 28, produced a starring performance in New Zealand's 34-10 semi-final win over Tonga on Saturday - only 23 days after breaking his forearm. He also shone in last month's NRL Grand Final, despite being on the losing side as Newcastle Knights were beaten 19-18 by Sydney Roosters. Dual-code international Waaka, 31, scored a hat-trick in New Zealand's 32-0 semi-final victory over Samoa. Waaka won a bronze medal in rugby union at the 2025 World Cup to go with two Olympic golds and a Commonwealth Games title in sevens. The award winners were announced in Brisbane, with several greats of the game selected as inaugural inductees into the IRL Hall of Legends. They included Sir Billy Boston - the first rugby league player to be knighted - Ellery Hanley, Malcolm Reilly, Alex Murphy, Neil Fox, Roger Millward and Mick Sullivan, the only Englishman to have won two World Cups.
